Title: Aminuddin challenges opposition to prove PH left development agenda unfinished
Article:
PORT DICKSON: Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has hit back at opposition leaders claiming they want to resume an unfinished development agenda under the Pakatan Harapan state administration.
The Negri Sembilan PH chairman challenged his rivals to present factual evidence of any project or plan that had allegedly stalled during PH's five-year tenure leading the state.
"What has been stalled? If they are merely copy-pasting what PH has already implemented, it means those initiatives have already been carried out.
"They can talk about an unfinished agenda, but what exactly is it? Prove it and put it in writing. Until today, they have failed to show anything that was left behind," he said after a house-to-house walkabout in Bandar Baru Sunggala today.
He was responding to Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who denied that BN was copying PH's manifesto, claiming instead that BN sought to continue a development agenda that had been interrupted.
Meanwhile, Aminuddin described the political dynamics between BN and Perikatan Nasional as a political drama designed to confuse voters for political gain.
"Everyone knows they appear to have no common ground, yet at the same time, they met frequently and worked together, which ultimately resulted in 11 seats being allocated for PN to contest," he said.

Title: German police hunt suspect after deadly car ramming near Berlin Gay Pride
Article:
BERLIN: German police searched on Sunday for a suspect believed linked to Islamist circles after a car ploughed into a crowd near Berlin's Gay Pride celebrations, killing one person and wounding 16 others.
The incident shattered what had been a day of celebration for hundreds of thousands attending Christopher Street Day, one of Europe's largest Pride events, and left revellers fleeing a central Berlin park as sirens echoed through the night.
Police told AFP the suspected vehicle was later found abandoned a few hundred metres from the heart of the festivities in Tiergarten park.
A manhunt involving helicopters and officers from several German states was under way across the capital on Sunday.
A suspect, believed to have links to "Islamist circles" had been "identified" but not yet arrested, police spokesman Florian Nath said.
An eyewitness near the main Pride stage at Brandenburg Gate told AFP that celebrations abruptly ended when police instructed people to leave.
"Go home, please," officers told participants as the crowd streamed away from the park, where emergency crews rushed to treat victims.
The attack occurred shortly before 10pm (2000 GMT) on Saturday.
"A vehicle entered the Tiergarten park and hit several people," police said.
One person died and 16 others were injured, including three with life-threatening injuries, according to Berlin fire department spokesman Dominik Pretz.
Around 30 more people were treated for shock at the scene.
Police spokesman Nath said investigators had identified a suspect but not yet made an arrest, adding that investigators believed he had links to "Islamist circles."
The search was widened to "the whole city" after the vehicle was discovered abandoned in the vast Tiergarten park.
The vehicle appeared to be "akin to a minivan or small SUV", Nath said.
The attack immediately revived memories of a series of deadly assaults that have shaken Germany in recent years and fuelled fierce debate over security.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed that those responsible would face justice.
In a statement, Merz described the incident as a "horrific act" and said he and Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt were being kept informed of developments.
Berlin Mayor Kai Wegner condemned what he called a brutal attack on "a gathering for a tolerant and peaceful Berlin."
Police had deployed more than 2,000 officers to secure the event.
Following the incident, additional personnel from across Germany joined the search operation, supported by helicopters equipped with thermal-imaging cameras.
An AFP journalist at the scene saw numerous emergency vehicles lining a nearby road and a large tent erected as police combed the area.
VIOLENT ATTACKS
Earlier Saturday, hundreds of thousands of people took part in the event, called Christopher Street Day in Germany, which is one of the biggest Pride events in Europe.
The march ended next to the Brandenburg Gate, which has been the venue for concerts since Friday.
Germany has in recent years seen several violent attacks at public spaces, including a stabbing in February 2025 at Berlin's Holocaust memorial, a stone's throw from the scene of Saturday's incident, in which a Spanish tourist was seriously injured.
A Syrian man named only as Wassim Al M. was jailed in March for 13 years for that attack, with the court finding he acted in the name of the so-called Islamic State group.
Last month Taleb Jawad al-Abdulmohsen, a 51-year-old Saudi psychiatrist, was sentenced to life in prison for killing six people and wounding more than 300.
He drove a rented SUV through a crowded Christmas market in 2024 in the easter city of Magdeburg.
Abdulmohsen was an anti-Islam activist and his testimony at his trial was sometimes incoherent and riddled with conspiracy theories and fringe far-right ideas.
The deadliest such attack in recent years was a truck rampage at a Berlin Christmas market in December 2016 that killed 12 people.
Saturday's incident came two months before voters in Berlin elect a new state assembly.
Polls indicate that the centre-right CDU, to which Merz and Wegner both belong, will face a stiff challenge from both the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) and the far-left Linke parties.
Wegner himself said earlier this month he would not run for re-election after months of criticism over his handling of a major blackout in January apparently caused by sabotage.

Title: Defence Ministry identifies asset procurements for G2G execution, says Khaled
Article:
PORT DICKSON: The Defence Ministry has identified several asset procurements to be carried out through government-to-government (G2G) arrangements.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the approach would enable Malaysia to secure competitive pricing while providing greater assurance of supply.
"In the past, we used open tenders where all companies could participate, whether they were original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), agents, or others.
"This time, however, we will carry out the procurement through G2G arrangements.
"Among its advantages, G2G procurement not only enables us to secure competitive pricing but also provides greater assurance of supply, as the commitments are backed by the governments with which we are dealing," he told reporters after attending the Kesejahteraan Warga ATM programme at Sirusa Camp here.
Khaled said two memoranda of understanding (MoUs) had been signed to facilitate G2G procurement — one with Turkiye and another with South Korea.
"Several countries, including Italy and France, have also proposed conducting procurement through G2G arrangements."
Khaled said several criteria were applied in selecting Malaysia's G2G partners for asset procurements.
"We want to ensure that the countries we engage with are trusted partners and are willing to transfer technology to Malaysia, helping us develop our domestic defence industry."
He said the most important consideration was that procurement specifications were determined by the respective armed services.
"What is most important is that the specifications are determined by our respective services — the Army, Navy and Air Force.
"It is not a case of the government purchasing equipment arbitrarily; rather, procurement is carried out in close consultation with the respective services that require the equipment."
Khaled said G2G procurement was also more transparent because it eliminated intermediaries, resulting in a clearer procurement process and more competitive pricing.
On Friday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had reduced the cost of acquiring Littoral Mission Ships (LMS) by
15 per cent
through direct G2G negotiations with Turkiye.
He said the G2G procurement approach eliminated reliance on intermediaries, whose commissions had previously inflated the cost of defence acquisitions.
Anwar said he personally raised the proposal with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, suggesting that negotiations be conducted directly between the two governments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid dismisses speculation of early general election
Article:
TAMPIN: There have been no discussions on the possibility of an early general election, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Responding to speculation that the next general election could be called ahead of schedule following claims of a growing "Blue Wave" in support of BN, Zahid said no such matter had been raised within the Unity Government.
"I have not had any discussions with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim about this.
"In the Unity Government, there are 18 parties, including five coalition blocs. If geopolitical circumstances change, of course the Prime Minister, as the head of government, will consider the appropriate timing and consult all parties," he told reporters after attending the Armed Forces Southern Zone Family Day at Kem Syed Sirajuddin, Gemas.
However, Zahid stressed that any decision to dissolve Parliament remained subject to the consent of His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
He described support for BN in the Negri Sembilan election campaign as an "organic Blue Wave", saying many voters were seeking a change in state leadership after two terms under the current administration.
He said the coalition believed Negri Sembilan required experienced leadership to spur economic growth, attract more investments and create better job opportunities for the people.
Responding to DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke's remarks that BN should avoid appearing overconfident, Zahid said there was nothing arrogant about offering voters an alternative government in Negri Sembilan.
"There is no arrogance in suggesting a change of government. Any political party or coalition that governs Negri Sembilan wants to remain in power, while those outside the government naturally want to take over.
"That is not arrogance. We should respond in a good and polite manner without resorting to personal attacks.
"Never go below the belt. That has always been my guiding principle," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six to be charged tomorrow over RM7mil PJ kidnapping
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Six men will be charged tomorrow over the kidnapping of a man for a RM7 million ransom in Petaling Jaya earlier this month.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said police have completed investigations into eight suspects linked to the July 17 case.
He said investigation papers were submitted to the Attorney-General's Chambers on July 24, which subsequently directed that six men be charged under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961.

Title: [UPDATED] 12 policemen arrested over alleged RM2mil extortion of Chinese citizen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Twelve policemen of various ranks have been arrested for allegedly extorting RM2 million from a Chinese citizen.
Sources said the victim was released after paying US$140,000 (about RM560,000) to the suspects.
The victim later lodged a report at the Dang Wangi district police headquarters, prompting an internal investigation.
It is understood that those arrested include officers holding the ranks of Deputy Superintendent and Assistant Superintendent, as well as rank-and-file personnel.
Sources said the group had allegedly demanded RM2 million from the victim, but he managed to pay only RM560,000 before deciding to report the matter to police.
Investigators have also recovered part of the money believed to be linked to the case.
When contacted, Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Sazalee Adam confirmed the arrests but did not elaborate further as investigations are ongoing.

Title: Muhyiddin breaks silence on Bersatu turmoil, alleges plot to remove him
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has spoken out on the party's leadership crisis, claiming former deputy president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin sought to remove him.
Muhyiddin said attempts to replace him as Bersatu president began after he stepped down as prime minister, but he remained in the position after receiving unanimous support from delegates at the party's annual general assembly in 2023.
He said he had initially intended to retire as party president but agreed to continue serving for one final term after members rejected his decision.
"I had expressed my intention to step down as president at the 2023 annual general assembly, but the delegates unanimously rejected it.
"To avoid disappointing party members, I decided to continue serving for this term, which will be my final term," he told Berita Harian in an interview.
Muhyiddin claimed that Hamzah, whom he had personally supported for the deputy presidency as part of a leadership succession plan, later became involved in efforts to pressure him to resign.
He said the move was contrary to the role of a deputy president, who was expected to support and assist the party president.
"I was given the mandate by the Supreme Leadership Council to prepare a succession plan. To ensure Bersatu remained strong, I named Hamzah as deputy president.
"Because of that, he won the position uncontested. Unfortunately, after winning the position, he acted against party discipline."
Muhyiddin alleged that a group of division leaders had been encouraged to call for his resignation, which he claimed was intended to allow Hamzah to become acting president without contesting for the top position.
"When I look back, perhaps this was the grand design from the beginning.
"He did not challenge me for the presidency, but obtained my endorsement to win the deputy presidency uncontested.
"Then a movement was created to remove me so he could become acting president. To me, this was not gentlemanly."
Muhyiddin said his efforts to strengthen Bersatu through a planned leadership transition failed, resulting in divisions within the party and forcing the leadership to take disciplinary action against several members and elected representatives.
He said the action taken against party members was a last resort after attempts to resolve the dispute internally had failed.
"If you ask me personally, I did not want disciplinary action to be taken against anyone.
"But violations of party discipline happened openly and extensively, causing division within the party. The action had to be taken to stabilise Bersatu."
On the growing rift between Bersatu and Pas, Muhyiddin maintained that Bersatu remained a legitimate member of Perikatan Nasional (PN), despite Pas ending its cooperation with the party.
He argued that a party which decided to sever ties with another member of a coalition should be the one to leave, rather than forcing the other party out.
"If we are unhappy with a friend in the same house, we should be the one to leave. We should not force our friend out."
Muhyiddin said the current situation had limited Bersatu's ability to use PN as its main political platform, particularly after Pas moved closer to Barisan Nasional in the Negri Sembilan election.
He said Bersatu would have to consider forming a new political arrangement with parties that shared similar views ahead of the next general election.
Muhyiddin also said he had begun informal discussions with several parties outside the current government bloc, questioning whether a unified opposition still existed after PN moved closer to BN.
"PN was previously the single opposition bloc in Parliament, but now it has cooperated with BN, which is part of the government.
"Today, Bersatu is among the parties that remain in opposition."
Asked about Bersatu's future leadership, Muhyiddin reiterated that his current term would be his final one as party president, as previously announced.
He said leadership changes would eventually take place to refresh the party and strengthen its position ahead of the next general election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RCI on Tabung Haji won't sway Negri Sembilan voters, says Zahid
Article:
TAMPIN: The government's move to release the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji will not affect voter sentiment in the Negri Sembilan election on Aug 1.
Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the issue should be viewed professionally and not be politicised during the campaign.
"I hope this issue is not politicised during the Negri Sembilan election. It should be viewed professionally.
"Any audit or investigation report should be used to find solutions, not to worsen the situation," he told reporters after attending the Armed Forces Southern Zone Family Day at Kem Syed Sirajuddin, Gemas.
Zahid said he supported the prime minister's intention to disclose the report and declassify it from the Official Secrets Act (OSA).
"This Wednesday, I am confident the prime minister will bring the matter before the Cabinet to decide whether these findings should be made public.
"As BN chairman, and with our eight ministers attending every Cabinet meeting, we support the move if the intention is to make the RCI report available to the public.
"The report must be declassified from the Official Secrets Act (OSA)," he said.
Zahid, who is also the deputy prime minister, added that no one would be immune from action if their names were implicated in the findings.
"The RCI is a Royal Commission established to conduct an investigation, and its report should be made known transparently.
"After that, if there are elements requiring further action, the appropriate legal processes can take place through the relevant enforcement agencies," he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Thursday, after opening a forum in Kuala Lumpur, said the government may release the final report of the RCI into Tabung Haji.
Anwar told reporters the report could be released immediately if Cabinet approval was not required, or after the Cabinet meets next Wednesday.

Title: Residents cash in on Dubai real estate cooldown amid Mideast war
Article:
DUBAI: Just over a year after moving to Dubai, Steve found himself moving unexpectedly up the property ladder, taking advantage of a cooling real estate market amid the Middle East war.
His new apartment is larger and closer to work than his previous resident, but the rent is nonetheless 15 per cent cheaper, he said, using a pseudonym due to Dubai's sensitivity on the matter.
When he arrived in Dubai in 2025, "it was really difficult to get a place in this area and the rents had gone up by a lot", said the 35-year-old, who works in the media sector.
Dubai's property market -- a pillar of its economy -- has soared in recent years, buoyed by the arrival of international high-net-worth individuals attracted by the glamorous lifestyle on offer in the emirate.
But the outbreak of the Middle East war in late February has dampened growth. Targets in Dubai came under fire in the early days of Iran's retaliation against US allies in the region.
Even some of its most iconic sites, such as Burj Al-Arab and the Palm Jumeirah, were not spared, dealing a blow to the city whose population is more than 90 per cent foreigners.
Hostilities resumed in July, following an April ceasefire, but Dubai has so far not been in the firing line.
But its image as a city that is "safe no matter what" has yet to recover from the blow it was dealt, said a real estate agent, speaking on condition of anonymity.
'Grey Area'
Today, she said, "we are in some sort of grey area. I'm getting a split sentiment; people think this has destabilised the region for a long time... And there are people who say this is the right time to invest."
Clients have not completely disappeared, the agent said, but the margins for negotiation have expanded.
"Since the war, the market's shifted from a seller's market to a buyer's market," she said.
British real estate consultancy Knight Frank said "we have already noted prices ebbing widely across the city's mainstream market by between five and 20 per cent, depending on location", after having surged by an average of 82.9 per cent since 2021.
The market has been hit previously, notably during the 2008 economic crisis and the Covid-19 pandemic.
Property giant Emaar nonetheless announced last month a massive $55 billion project in the heart of Dubai, hoping to attract some 150,000 residents, signalling its confidence in the market's ability to bounce back.
Binghatti, another major developer, said it had sold two luxury apartments in the centre in June, at $54 million and $19 million respectively.
According to a report by the Betterhomes agency, based on official figures, sales transaction values fell in the second quarter of 2026 by 45 per cent year on year, with the luxury sector hit particularly hard.
But chief executive Richard Waind nonetheless insisted that the situation has improved over the past weeks.
"We're starting to see demand increase again through June and then into this month, both in terms of buyer activity and buyer deals happening," he told AFP.
Demand is mainly driven by Dubai residents, rather than foreign investors, he said.
But, he explained, this time of year has traditionally been a lull period and projected that investment would begin to "recover and return as we come out of the summer".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah Immigration denies viral claim of Filipino detainee deaths in overcrowded depots
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah Immigration Department has refuted social media claims alleging that numerous Filipino detainees died due to overcrowding at the state's detention depots.
State Immigration director Datuk SH Sitti Saleha Habib Yussof said the allegations were false, baseless, and misleading, adding that a viral photograph linked to the claim was not taken at any immigration detention depot in Sabah.
"All Filipino detainees housed at the immigration detention depots in Sabah are in good condition while awaiting repatriation to their home country," she said in a statement today.
She said throughout their detention, all detainees are provided with appropriate care and protection in accordance with the law and established standard operating procedures.
Sitti Saleha said detainees receive basic necessities, including meals served on a fixed schedule that adhere to nutritional standards approved by the Health Ministry for both adults and children.
She added that detainees are also granted access to necessary medical treatment and other essential needs.
Addressing delays in the repatriation process, Sitti Saleha noted that sea transfers from Sandakan to Zamboanga — the primary route — had been suspended by Philippine authorities since February.
"To ensure that repatriation continues, the Sabah Immigration Department is using alternative routes, namely flights from Kota Kinabalu to Manila and sea transport from Lahad Datu to Bongao.
"However, repatriation through these alternative routes is subject to the detainees' families agreeing to bear the travel costs," she said.
She reiterated the department's commitment to safeguarding the welfare, safety, and health of all detainees while executing repatriations strictly according to legal procedures and in close cooperation with Philippine authorities.
Sitti Saleha also advised the public against sharing or believing unverified and misleading information, photos, or content, urging them to rely solely on the Immigration Department's official channels for accurate updates.

Title: Malaysia remains Scoot's key market on robust travel demand: Chief commercial officer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia remains a key market for Scoot, the low-cost carrier of the Singapore Airlines (SIA) Group, driven by sustained demand for leisure and business travel, the airline's chief commercial officer Calvin Chan said.
He said Scoot now serves 12 destinations in Malaysia, mounting 130 weekly flights between both countries.
Chan said the airline has also widened its regional footprint in Southeast Asia, flying to at least half a dozen new destinations and increasing frequencies to places it is already flying to.
As at the end of June 2026, Scoot operated a network of 85 destinations across 18 countries and territories, he told Bernama in a recent interview.
The airline currently operates more than 60 aircraft, comprising 24 Boeing 787 Dreamliners, 30 Airbus A320 family aircraft and nine Embraer E190-E2 jets.
For the financial year ended March 31, 2026, Scoot flew more than 2.2 million passengers to and from its Malaysian destinations, representing approximately a 14 per cent year-on-year increase.
He said that brisk tourist arrivals from the Visit Malaysia 2026 campaign also help make Malaysia a vibrant destination, despite intense competition in the low-cost carrier segment.
These factors have combined to generate strong demand for air travel between Malaysia and Singapore, he said.
Malaysia continues to play a strategic role in the airline's network, supported by Putrajaya's close economic and social ties with Singapore.
He said Malaysia serves as an important source of both point-to-point traffic and connecting passengers into the wider SIA Group network via Singapore.
Tourist arrivals remain particularly robust, with Malaysia continuing to be a top travel destination for Singaporean travellers.
"In the first two months of 2026, 3.4 million Singaporean visitors travelled to Malaysia, accounting for nearly half of total international tourist arrivals," he said.
To date, the 12 destinations Scoot serves in Malaysia include Ipoh, Kota Bahru, Kota Kinabalu, Kuala Lumpur, Kuantan, Kuching, Langkawi, Melaka, Miri, Penang, Sibu and Subang.
This makes Scoot the only foreign airline serving the highest number of destinations in Malaysia.
Chan said the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore route continues to be one of the world's busiest international air corridors, with demand remaining resilient across both leisure and business travel segments.
He said Malaysia's tourism prospects are expected to receive a further boost from the Visit Malaysia 2026 campaign, with Scoot well positioned to support the country's tourism ambitions through its extensive regional network.
To capitalise on the expected growth, Scoot entered a three-year strategic partnership with Tourism Malaysia in August 2025 to jointly promote the country across key markets, including Singapore, China, Australia and Indonesia.
He said the collaboration, which runs until 2028, aims to drive international visitor arrivals through joint marketing initiatives with tourism stakeholders.
Chan added that Scoot currently operates seven weekly flights to Subang using Airbus A320 family aircraft and will continue evaluating opportunities to expand its presence in Malaysia based on travel demand, operational considerations and its broader network strategy.
Southeast Asia remains growth engine
Beyond Malaysia, Chan said Southeast Asia will continue to be Scoot's primary growth engine over the next few years, underpinned by rising disposable incomes, expanding airport infrastructure and travellers' growing preference for affordable short-haul travel.
He said the airline has steadily expanded its regional footprint over the past year.
During that period, Scoot launched services to Chiang Rai and Palembang in January, followed by Medan and Tokyo Haneda in February and March, before adding Belitung and Pontianak in Indonesia during May and June.
Scoot also increased flight frequencies to several destinations across the region, including Bali, Jakarta, Labuan Bajo, Lombok, Manado, Phuket and Sibu, while boosting services to Changsha, Okinawa and Vienna in response to growing demand.
Chan said the airline will continue pursuing disciplined, demand-led expansion across short, medium and long-haul markets while maintaining a commercially sustainable and diversified network.
Fleet and digital investments
Touching on its fleet, Chan said the Embraer E190-E2 aircraft enables Scoot to serve secondary cities and airports with infrastructure constraints while complementing its larger Airbus A320 family and Boeing 787 fleets.
In May this year, Scoot announced a firm order for five Airbus A320neo family aircraft and exercised options for an additional six, bringing its total A320neo family orderbook to 20 aircraft.
The additional aircraft, scheduled for progressive delivery from 2028, would provide greater flexibility to deploy capacity across regional markets, launch new routes and strengthen connectivity into the wider SIA Group network, said Chan.
While Scoot's Boeing 787 Dreamliners remain central to its medium- and long-haul operations covering destinations in Australia, North Asia, North India, the Middle East and Europe, Chan said there are no immediate plans to expand the airline's widebody fleet.
Beyond network and fleet expansion, Scoot will continue investing in digitalisation and artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance operational efficiency and improve customer experience.
Among the initiatives are enhancements to its AI-powered virtual assistant Marvie, expanded self-service capabilities at airports, AI-supported customer service functions and technology-driven operational systems designed to improve productivity, strengthen disruption management and deliver a more seamless travel experience.

Title: Malaysian agritech startup Qarbotech expands global footprint
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian agritech startup Qarbotech is expanding its global footprint, with its technology, QarboGrow, a carbon quantum dot-based photosynthesis enhancer, now being used by nearly 7,500 farmers worldwide.
Qarbotech commercialises QarboGrow, its flagship product, which was developed through research in Malaysia and is designed to improve plants' ability to utilise sunlight more efficiently.
Qarbotech co-founder and chief executive officer Chor Chee Hoe said QarboGrow recorded nearly RM3 million in sales last year, with a large share generated from overseas markets.
Chor said the company is conducting pilot trials in Japan, with prospective customers considering purchases if the trials are successful.
"We already have the large-scale manufacturing facility here in Malaysia, so we are looking to work with more distributors and enter different markets," he told Bernama at a recognition ceremony hosted by the Japanese Embassy here recently.
The ceremony was held to celebrate Qarbotech's victory at the SusHi Tech Challenge 2026 Global Startup Pitch Competition in Tokyo.
Founded in 2018, Qarbotech won the Grand Prize after emerging as the top entry from more than 800 applicants representing over 60 countries.
The company received 10 million Japanese yen (about US$61,000) in prize money.
According to Chor, the company is also seeking distributors in India and exploring opportunities in other markets.
"QarboGrow is currently sold in Malaysia, Thailand and China. Our biggest market right now, in terms of the number of farmers using our technology, is China," said Chor.
Chor said adoption in Malaysia remained relatively slow because the company mainly reaches smallholders and has yet to secure a strong anchor distributor capable of serving medium-sized and larger plantations.
"In Malaysia, adoption is quite slow because organically, we have successfully penetrated smallholder farming communities," he said.
"For medium-sized and bigger plantations, we don't have significant access because we have yet to secure strong anchor distributors in Malaysia," he said.
To widen domestic adoption, Qarbotech has worked with government agencies, including the Departments of Agriculture in Penang, Terengganu and Kelantan.
Chor said the collaboration enabled the company to introduce its technology to nearly 1,200 rice farmers.
He said such initiatives could help accelerate adoption, as QarboGrow remained a relatively new product and most farmers were more familiar with conventional agricultural inputs such as fertilisers and pesticides.
Qarbotech hopes to collaborate more closely with the Department of Agriculture and participate in its nationwide roadshows to educate farmers about photosynthesis-enhancing technology and its potential applications.
"We hope that we can join forces with them to educate farmers about the technology behind QarboGrow and show them what is possible," Chor said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: Students need patriotism, digital literacy to navigate modern challenges
Article:
JEMPOL: Secondary school students must be continuously nurtured with patriotism and equipped with digital literacy to face modern challenges.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said an emphasis on nationhood and history is crucial to ensuring every citizen understands their responsibility in advancing the country.
"As a son or daughter of this nation, as a citizen, we also have responsibilities and must understand our history, as well as our roles and duties in becoming Malaysians who can help move the country forward.
"I also took the opportunity to listen to questions and views from the Form Six students, and I found that most of them are highly motivated and understand current challenges, including fake news, mental health issues, and social media. Many also asked about the future amid the rapid growth of technology, including artificial intelligence (AI)," he said.
He said this after meeting 60 Form Six students following a dialogue session held in conjunction with the Pentarama X Kelab Malaysiaku programme and the Safe Internet Campaign at the Jempol District Information Office today.
Organised by the Information Department (JaPen), the programme brought together students from Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Batu Kikir, SMK Seri Perpatih, and SMK Datuk Mansor in the Jempol parliamentary constituency.
Also present were JaPen director-general Erwin Khairul Ahmad and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) Negri Sembilan director Faisal Hamdi Mohammed Ghouth.
Fahmi said the programme, which adopts an edutainment approach, not only enhances National Month celebrations but also serves as an interactive platform for ministry leaders to listen to youth aspirations.
Meanwhile, Erwin Khairul said the Pentarama X Kelab Malaysiaku initiative has been expanded to promote messages of independence, unity, and preparations for National Day and Malaysia Day at the school level.
He said there are currently 850 Kelab Malaysiaku operating nationwide.
Pentarama is a performance unit under JaPen that communicates government policies, official information, and patriotic values through song, dance, and drama.

Title: Online extremists exploit lonely youths' search for friendship, belonging
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Feelings of loneliness, isolation and having no one to turn to are making teenagers and children increasingly vulnerable to online radicalisation and emerging threats such as Nihilistic Violent Extremism (NVE).
Unlike conventional terrorist groups driven by political or religious ideologies, NVE is characterised by a belief that life, society or existing systems have no inherent value or meaning, with violence viewed as a means to cause destruction, fear or chaos.
The threat has drawn international attention, with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) tracking more than 350 individuals linked to NVE investigations in the United States in February.
In Southeast Asia, an armed attack at a school in the Philippines on June 22, which killed three students and injured 20 others, was linked to NVE after two suspects, aged 14 and 15, were allegedly influenced by extreme online content.
International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) Centre for Peace, Dialogue and Xenophobia Studies deputy director Dr Ahmad El-Muhammady said that while NVE shared similarities with other forms of extremism in its acceptance of violence, its underlying drivers were significantly different.
"The common thread is the acceptance of violence. They believe violence is a way to solve problems and express suppressed anger and revenge.
"They also glorify individuals who choose violent paths, such as school or mass shooters and perpetrators of knife attacks," he told Berita Harian.
He said NVE particularly affected younger people facing psychological stress, bullying, social isolation or emotional struggles, with social media, video games and other online platforms providing avenues for exposure and influence.
Ahmad said that unlike groups such as the Islamic State which use religious or political narratives to justify violence, NVE was driven largely by psychological factors and personal discontent.
"While ideological elements may exist, they are less dominant than psychological stress and frustration. In NVE, it is not merely about being a bullying victim, but a dominant internal orientation towards violence as a form of expression," he said.
He said repeated exposure to content that normalised violence could influence how individuals processed emotions and perceived violent behaviour.
"When violence is normalised, it distorts how individuals view these actions," he said, adding that excessive immersion in online platforms and video games could also blur the line between virtual and real-world experiences.
He stressed that NVE must be addressed holistically, taking into account psychological factors, family dynamics, social environments, peer influence and evolving digital culture.
Southeast Asia Regional Centre for Counter-Terrorism (SEARCCT) director-general Datin Paduka Nur Ashikin Mohd Taib said extremist groups were increasingly exploiting the loneliness and isolation experienced by young people by offering attention, friendship and a sense of belonging.
She said youths were typically not targeted at random but were often those who felt rejected, sidelined or friendless and were searching for acceptance online.
"Some teenagers feel rejected, sidelined and friendless, ultimately seeking connections online. When someone pays attention to them, offers praise or makes them feel valued, they are easily drawn in because they feel accepted as part of that community," she said.
She said recruitment often began with seemingly harmless interactions during online gaming or messaging sessions before developing into closer relationships.
Recruiters would then gradually introduce violent or extremist content, causing victims to become desensitised and eventually view previously unacceptable beliefs and actions as normal.
"Previously, they approached targets in person, but now everything happens online through social media, video games and communication applications. When repeatedly exposed to extreme content, actions initially viewed as wrong are eventually seen as normal," she said.
Nur Ashikin said extremist groups understood that teenagers were often more susceptible to emotional support than financial incentives, using attention, praise and a sense of belonging to build trust before manipulating their thinking.
"More worryingly, radicalisation is now occurring much faster. Reports show that an individual can be influenced within a short period if interactions are intensive," she said.
She said recruiters also exploited online gaming ecosystems that allowed players to communicate, including sandbox and combat-oriented games, to establish personal connections with potential victims.
Recruiters would then move targets to private chat groups on platforms such as Telegram or WhatsApp, initially discussing shared interests and hobbies before identifying impressionable individuals.
"These individuals are then brought into closed groups. Most recruiters use fake accounts and anonymous identities, leaving many unaware that they are being manipulated.
"As the relationship deepens, they begin influencing the victim's mindset towards violence and specific ideologies," she said.
Nur Ashikin said preventing and countering violent extremism required a whole-of-society approach involving parents, schools, communities, religious institutions, civil society organisations and digital platform providers.
She said efforts should focus on strengthening digital literacy, providing emotional support and building resilience among young people.
"Early awareness, digital literacy, emotional support and community involvement are essential in building youth resilience. In many cases, prevention is far better than taking action after someone has fallen under the influence of extremist ideologies," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN-BN pact puts Negri Sembilan people's interests above differences, says Samsuri
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The pact between Perikatan Nasional and Barisan Nasional in the Negri Sembilan election puts the interests of the people above all differences, says Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar.
The PN chairman said this was demonstrated through the coalition's supplementary offers, which were designed to complement the manifesto presented by BN for the state election.
Samsuri, who is also Pas vice-president and Terengganu Menteri Besar, said it is a joint effort between PN and BN to form a stable, trustworthy, and capable state government in Negri Sembilan.
In calling on the public to build new hope and create a brighter future for Negri Sembilan, he stressed that a manifesto is not merely a promise, but a trust that must be fulfilled.
"PN has presented 14 additional offers centred on six key areas, namely administration, youth and family, economy, welfare, education, and employment. Each commitment has been formulated realistically and responsibly, taking into account the state's financial capacity and the actual needs of the people.
"This encompasses various aspects, ranging from the cost of living and housing to quality job opportunities, economic development, and the welfare of a multiracial and multi-religious society," he said in a statement today.
Yesterday, PN launched 14 additional offers across six core pillars under the theme 'PN Sepakat Hebatkan Negeri Sembilan' ahead of the state election. The six pillars cover administration, youth, the economy, welfare, education, and employment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australia exempts Asean students from visa fee hike in bid to deepen regional ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Australia has carved out an exemption for students from Asean nations after raising its international student visa fee by 25 per cent.
Assistant Minister for International Education Julian Hill said the exemption was a deliberate policy choice tied to the country's engagement with the region, according to the Straits Times.
"A reduced visa fee rate for students from Asean nations reflects the importance Australia places on welcoming high-quality students from Southeast Asia," he said.
Canberra raised the non-refundable visa application fee from A$2,000 to A$2,500 on July 3, but students from Asean countries were subject only to an inflation-adjusted increase of A$50, bringing their fee to A$2,050 — the first time such a distinction has been made.
"Australia and Asean nations share deep, abiding bonds and it's important that our young people spend time in their formative years getting to know each other and building lifelong bonds," Hill added.
The latest increase is part of a series of hikes aimed at managing a surge in migration since the Covid-19 pandemic. The fee had previously risen from A$710 to A$1,600 in July 2024 and further to A$2,000 in July 2025.
Australia already maintained a lower fee of A$745 for students from Pacific nations, including Timor-Leste, which joined Asean in October 2025, as part of its diplomatic outreach to the region.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump faces midterm reckoning with 100 days to US vote
Article:
WASHINGTON: One hundred days before the US midterm elections, President Donald Trump's Republicans are staring down polling that points to the loss of the House of Representatives and a ferocious battle to retain the Senate.
Trump will not appear on the ballot on Nov 3, but the stakes for his presidency could hardly be higher.
A Democratic House would give the party control of powerful committees and subpoena authority, likely subjecting Trump's administration to two years of investigations and potentially exposing him to a third impeachment drive.
Republicans enter the final stretch with a historically narrow House majority, weak presidential approval ratings and an electorate increasingly unhappy about living costs and the grinding war with Iran.
US elections website Decision Desk HQ predicts that the Democratic Party has a 59-per cent chance of winning the House, forecasting a 224-211 majority.
The president's party usually loses ground in midterm elections, and only a handful of seats need to change hands.
Gasoline prices have climbed above $4 a gallon as the Iran war disrupts energy markets, inflation remains elevated and interest rates are high.
Polling cited by Democrats suggests voters now trust them more than Republicans on inflation, health care and even immigration, long considered a Republican strength.
"Donald Trump and Republicans have failed the American people," House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said Thursday, announcing an affordability campaign built around groceries, gasoline, housing and health care.
'WORK TO DO'
Republicans insist the election will offer a choice between what Speaker Mike Johnson calls "common sense" and an increasingly progressive Democratic Party.
They plan to highlight border enforcement and tax cuts while portraying Democratic candidates as aligned with the socialist left.
Trump is pressing every available advantage.
He has waged a prolonged campaign for congressional Republicans to pass the SAVE America Act, which he portrays as essential to preventing election fraud but Democrats condemn as an attempt to suppress legitimate votes.
Republicans have been considerably more successful in another effort to shape the electorate: redrawing congressional maps.
Both parties have tried to carve out new safe seats, but Republicans look likely to emerge with a net advantage of between five and 12 seats.
That could offset the national political environment in a House contest expected to be decided by a similarly narrow margin.
Sarah Binder, a politics professor at George Washington University, said the redistricting arms race had been particularly consequential in this cycle, with fewer than one in 20 House races genuine toss-ups.
"Redistricting has really pared back the grounds on which Democrats can contest those seats," she told AFP.
Republicans also hold a substantial financial advantage, with party campaign committees and allied groups entering the final months with tens of millions of dollars more than their Democratic counterparts.
'VERY SMALL FAVOURITES'
The Senate presents a different but equally dramatic contest.
Republicans hold a 53-47 majority, meaning Democrats need a net gain of four seats. Decision Desk HQ narrowly favors Republicans to retain control through a 50-50 split, with Vice President JD Vance casting tie-breaking votes.
For Trump, even a divided Washington – with Democrats controlling the House and Republicans holding the Senate – would transform the remainder of his term.
His legislative agenda would stall in the House, his officials would face inquiries and public hearings, and Democrats would gain a national platform from which to scrutinize the Iran war, administration ethics and the president's attempts to reshape elections.
Political analyst Chuck Todd said in a podcast marking 100 days until the midterms that Republicans had gone from "clear favorites" in the Senate nine months ago to "very small favorites."
House elections, he said, would likely yield a 10 to 25-seat Democratic advantage, pointing to Trump's persistent low polling.
The president's popularity remains near record lows in a new Economist/YouGov survey, with 36 percent of Americans saying they approve of his performance as president.
"There is no better predictor of a midterm than presidential job approval. A president's job approval under 45 guarantees their party is going to lose seats. It doesn't mean they'll lose chambers, but they definitely lose seats," the former news anchor said.
"A president under 40 – they're going to lose chambers. The question is, how bad is it? How big is the wave going to be?"
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rescuers scour South China Sea for 23 missing after Vietnamese vessel sinks
Article:
HONG KONG: Rescuers were searching for 23 people missing after a Vietnamese ship sank in the busy waterway of the South China Sea, while 39 were pulled from the waters, China's state broadcaster CCTV said.
Authorities in the southern province of Hainan said the cargo vessel Khoi Nguyen 18, with 62 Vietnamese nationals aboard, ran into distress in waters near Fiery Cross Reef, CCTV added.
A distress flare from the vessel was first spotted by a Chinese rescue ship, the Nanhai Jiu 115, on Saturday evening, CCTV said.
Six Chinese vessels, a rescue helicopter, and a Vietnamese vessel joined the search and rescue effort at the site, it said.
The Vietnamese-registered vessel is nearly 70m (230 ft) long with a gross tonnage of 999 tons.
The area around the reef is part of the disputed Spratly Islands, which China calls the Nansha Islands, a group of highly contested reefs, islets, and atolls in the resource-rich South China Sea.
China claims sovereignty over almost the entire strategic waterway, including the Spratly Islands, where it has built runways and militarised artificial islands.
But Beijing's sweeping claims overlap with those of Vietnam, the Philippines, Taiwan, Malaysia, and Brunei.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aeon's legal setback unlikely to hurt operations: MBSB Research
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Court of Appeal's ruling in Aeon Co (M) Bhd's property dispute is unlikely to have a material impact on the retailer's operations, MBSB Research said.
The appellate court upheld the High Court's decision ordering Aeon to pay Betanaz Properties Sdn Bhd RM18.68 million plus interest, while dismissing Betanaz's larger RM59.3 million claim.
Aeon's counterclaim against Betanaz and Ahmad Zaki Resources Bhd was also dismissed.
Aeon said it will seek leave to appeal to the Federal Court and file an application to stay the execution of the judgment.
MBSB Research noted that the RM18.68 million judgment sum and accrued interest of RM3.6 million as at Jan 22, 2025 have already been deposited into a stakeholder account.
"Hence, the latest incremental exposure should mainly comprise interest from Jan 23 onwards and Court of Appeal legal costs," it said.
Under the ruling, Aeon must pay RM60,000 in legal costs to Betanaz and RM30,000 to Ahmad Zaki, while Betanaz is required to pay RM50,000 to Aeon, resulting in a net legal cost of RM40,000.
Assuming interest accrues at five per cent a year, MBSB Research estimated additional interest of about RM1.4 million from Jan 23, 2025 to July 2026.
Including the net legal costs, the total incremental financial impact is estimated at RM1.44 million, equivalent to just one per cent of the research house's financial year 2026 (FY26) core earnings forecast for Aeon.
"On a FY26-only accrual basis, interest from Jan 1, 2026 to July 22, 2026 would amount to RM520,000, or 0.4 per cent of FY26 core profit after tax and non-controlling interests.
"For FY27, if the matter is further stayed and interest continues to accrue, every additional full year of interest would amount to RM930,000, or 0.6 per cent of FY27 core earnings," it said.
MBSB Research kept its "Buy" call on Aeon with an unchanged target price of RM1.47.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Higher Sara allocation could ease cost pressures, says expert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A higher Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) allocation could provide immediate relief to lower-income households grappling with rising living costs, but the assistance should remain a temporary safety net rather than a long-term solution.
Faculty of Business and Management senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said a higher Sara allocation would help vulnerable families cope with essential expenses such as food and daily necessities, while also generating a positive multiplier effect as the assistance is spent within the domestic economy.
"The proposed increase in the Sara allocation should be viewed as a targeted short-term intervention to ease cost-of-living pressures, particularly for lower-income households.
"Direct assistance such as Sara can provide immediate relief by helping families manage essential expenses, especially food and daily necessities.
"It can also generate a positive multiplier effect as the assistance is spent within the domestic economy," he told the New Straits Times.
However, Idham said the effectiveness of the programme would depend on whether the assistance was accurately targeted and sufficient to offset rising living costs.
"Sara should be seen as a social safety net rather than a permanent solution to address the broader cost-of-living challenge."
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim recently announced that the government would increase the Sara allocation in the near future, although details of the
revised assistance
have yet to be announced.
The Sara assistance is channelled through recipients' MyKad, allowing eligible individuals to purchase essential goods.
It covers the purchase of essential items such as food staples, household products, hygiene items, health-related goods and school supplies, aimed at helping eligible recipients manage the cost of living.
On how the government could finance the increase, Idham said any additional allocation must be supported by prudent fiscal planning to avoid placing unnecessary pressure on public finances.
He said the government could reprioritise existing expenditure, reduce less effective programmes, strengthen tax compliance, improve revenue collection and capitalise on stronger economic growth instead of relying on additional borrowing.
"The government should avoid excessive reliance on new borrowing to finance recurring assistance, as this may create greater pressure on public finances and limit fiscal flexibility in the future."
While welcoming additional financial assistance, Idham stressed that it should be accompanied by structural reforms to address the root causes of rising living costs.
He said the government should focus on raising incomes through better wages, improving productivity, creating higher-value jobs and reducing major household expenses such as food, housing, transportation and healthcare.
"A sustainable approach requires addressing the root causes of cost-of-living pressures rather than relying solely on financial assistance."
Idham also called for regular reviews of the Sara programme based on inflation, household income trends and the country's fiscal position to ensure it remained sustainable and well targeted.
"The programme should continue to use accurate data to ensure assistance reaches those who genuinely need it, while the government develops a long-term strategy to reduce dependence on financial aid by improving economic opportunities and household earning capacity."
On July 19, Anwar said the government was considering increasing the allocation for the
Sara initiative
under Budget 2027, subject to the country's economic position.
He said he had discussed the matter with Treasury secretary-general Datuk Johan Mahmood Merican to assess the feasibility of increasing the assistance to ease the people's burden.
The Sara initiative is part of the government's efforts to provide assistance for essential goods to eligible recipients, complementing other measures to address the rising cost of living.
Sara allocations have risen to RM15 billion in 2026, from RM10 billion in 2024.
Under the Sara Untuk Semua initiative, some 22 million people, or 87 per cent of all recipients, generated over RM1.77 billion in local market transactions this year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang sees rise in consumer claims as awareness of redress rights grows
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Consumer awareness in Penang of the right to seek redress through the Tribunal for Consumer Claims Malaysia (TTPM) is on the rise, with the number of claims filed showing an upward trend in recent years.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry Penang director S. Jegan said 614 claims were filed in 2024, rising to 777 cases last year, while 444 claims were recorded in the first six months of this year as of June 30.
"The increase in claims filed over the past few years shows that the public is becoming more aware of their rights as consumers and knows the proper channel to seek redress.
"This is a very positive development as it reflects the growing level of consumer awareness in Penang of their rights under the Consumer Protection Act 1999, while also indicating that the ministry's advocacy and public awareness efforts have been successful in improving public understanding of the role of the TTPM," he said.
However, he acknowledged that some consumers are still unaware that they can bring disputes involving compensation claims before the TTPM without going through complicated court proceedings.
He said some consumers are also reluctant to file claims despite being entitled to do so, as they perceive the tribunal process to be difficult and costly.
"In reality, the TTPM process is simple, fast and requires only an RM5 processing fee. The tribunal serves as an effective alternative avenue for resolving consumer disputes without having to go through lengthy court proceedings," he said.
Jegan said the most common claims filed in the state involve home renovation works and beauty treatment services, while a significant number of complaints also relate to the purchase of electrical appliances and furniture.
He said home renovation complaints typically involve delays in project completion, unsatisfactory workmanship or contractors failing to comply with agreement terms. Claims involving beauty treatment services generally concern services that do not match what was promised, treatment side effects or packages that differ from those advertised.
He added that main factors prompting consumers to bring cases before the tribunal include traders' failure to provide refunds, the supply of goods that do not meet promised specifications, and breaches of contract.
Jegan said 262 cases were resolved as of June 30 this year, while 775 of the 777 claims filed last year have been settled, with the remaining two cases still pending following postponement applications by the claimants.
To address recurring issues, he said the ministry has stepped up advocacy and public awareness programmes, intensified monitoring and enforcement against traders, and conducted engagement sessions with industry players to ensure compliance with the law while safeguarding consumer rights.
"One of the common mistakes consumers make when filing claims is failing to submit complete supporting documents, such as purchase receipts, contracts or agreements, proof of payment and details of the party against whom the claim is made," he said.
He advised consumers to keep all documents related to their transactions in a safe place to facilitate the claims process should any dispute arise.
Jegan also reminded traders to conduct business transparently, comply with the specifications of products and services offered, and respect consumer rights to avoid disputes being brought before the tribunal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Strong winds and rain lash China after Typhoon Noul makes landfall
Article:
BEIJING: Typhoon Noul made landfall in China early Sunday morning, state media reported, lashing a stretch of the southern coast with strong winds and rain in the fiercest storm to hit the country this year.
Severe weather forecasts for Noul had spurred authorities to evacuate more than 340,000 people and suspend work and rail services, with major flight disruptions continuing throughout Sunday morning.
The centre of the typhoon crossed over land at around 3:50 am (1950 GMT) near the town of Pinghai, Guangdong Province – about 80 kilometres northeast of financial hub Hong Kong – state broadcaster CCTV reported.
Maximum sustained winds near the eye of the storm at the time of landfall were 162 kilometres (101 miles) an hour, the report said.
That made Noul the strongest typhoon to strike the country so far in 2026, CCTV added.
Battering winds and heavy rains were seen in footage published by CCTV Sunday, with roads strewn with debris and some small structures including a basketball net toppled by the gusts.
At least 350 passenger flights departing and arriving from Hong Kong had been cancelled on Sunday, the airport's website showed.
Hong Kong had issued its second-highest storm signal, T9, overnight, but it was replaced by the T8 signal in the morning.
"Noul is moving steadily into inland Guangdong and weakening progressively, but gales are still affecting many places over Hong Kong, with occasional storm force winds over high ground," the Hong Kong Observatory said.
The Hong Kong government said it has received over 100 reports of fallen trees, and nine people were injured.
"After landfall, Noul will move inland, bringing strong winds and rain to Jiangxi, Hunan and Hubei provinces," CCTV said.
The report noted that precipitation caused by the typhoon could last through Tuesday, including in provinces as far north as Henan and Shandong.
Authorities in Guangdong elevated the province's disaster relief emergency response to its third-highest level on Sunday morning.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN rejects racial rhetoric, insists NS polls cooperation won't alter party's stance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional has stressed that its political cooperation in the Negri Sembilan election will not come at the expense of its long-held principles, while rejecting racial rhetoric and "politics of fear" as having no place in building a united Malaysia.
In a statement today, BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the coalition remained committed to its principles despite its political understanding forged for the state polls.
"BN wishes to stress that the political understanding and cooperation established for the Negri Sembilan election does not in any way mean BN will compromise its principles or accept the political narratives of any party.
"BN remains steadfast in standing by its own principles," he said.
Zambry said BN's strength lay in its multiracial power-sharing model, which had helped develop Malaysia for more than six decades through mutual respect, moderation and political stability.
He said this track record continued to underpin the coalition's commitment to preserving national harmony and progress.
At the same time, Zambry said BN would not tolerate statements that inflamed racial sentiments, questioned the place of any community as part of Malaysia or created unnecessary anxiety among the people.
"After nearly seven decades of independence, politics that divides Malaysians along racial lines has no place in building a united nation."
He also took aim at what he described as "politics of fear", accusing certain quarters of attempting to convince voters that a particular race would be threatened if certain political partnerships formed the government.
"Politics of fear is dangerous because it breeds suspicion, prejudice and hatred."
Zambry said BN would continue to champion moderation, stability and national unity while remaining committed to upholding the Federal Constitution, the Rukun Negara and the country's constitutional framework.
He said this included safeguarding Islam as the religion of the Federation, the institution of the Malay Rulers, the special position of the Malays and Bumiputera, as well as the legitimate rights of all Malaysians.
"These are the foundations that have united the country since independence, and they must continue to be defended."
Zambry added that BN rejected those who sought to build "racial walls" and instead would continue offering leadership that built "bridges of unity", strengthened public confidence and promoted a shared future for all Malaysians.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kerjaya's data centre win opens door to more M&E jobs, says Kenanga
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd's recent subcontract win for a data centre project in the Klang Valley could pave the way for more mechanical and electrical (M&E) jobs in the fast-growing sector, Kenanga Research said.
Although the project's expected net margin of six per cent is below Kerjaya's typical 10 per cent range, the research house said the lower margin is offset by the project's short six-month construction period.
"We remain positive as this is a fast-track, six-month project that simultaneously opens up new M&E tenders in the future. While this contract value is relatively small, we welcome this maiden M&E contract win, opening new M&E job opportunities in the buoyant data centre space," it said in a note.
Kerjaya's unit, Kerjaya Prospek (M) Sdn Bhd, secured a RM52.5 million lump-sum subcontract for civil, structural and basic low-voltage M&E works involving a new 275-kilovolt consumer landing station serving a data centre in the Klang Valley.
The client's identity was not disclosed due to a non-disclosure agreement.
The latest contract lifts Kerjaya's year-to-date job wins to RM2.15 billion, close to Kenanga Research's full-year target of RM2.3 billion. Its outstanding order book now stands at RM5.05 billion, providing earnings visibility over the next three years.
"We maintain our financial year 2026 job replenishment target of RM2.3 billion, while management is expected to reveal a new target in the upcoming briefing next month.
"Moving forward, the pipeline remains supported by a healthy building tender book of RM2 billion and RM3 billion," it said.
Beyond this, Kerjaya is also eyeing up to RM2 billion worth of infrastructure packages at Andaman Island and is participating in the tender for the Penang LRT Package 2.
Kenanga Research kept its "Outperform" call on the stock with a target price of RM2.85.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tok Mat defends BN's record on Indian community
Article:
REMBAU: Negri Sembilan Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan has defended his administration's record, highlighting several initiatives implemented for the Indian community during his tenure as menteri besar.
He said among the key measures was a housing policy for estate workers forced to leave plantations following changes in the sector.
Mohamad said the state government had developed dedicated housing areas to ensure affected workers continued to have a place to live.
"We introduced a housing policy specifically for estate workers.
"It was not meant for outsiders. It was for estate workers who had to leave the plantations. Many of them had lived there for two or three generations, but had to move out because the rubber plantations were no longer operating.
"What would have happened to them if we had not helped? That is why I built houses for them," he said.
He was speaking at a programme with the Indian community at Taman Intan, Rantau, last night.
Mohamad said his administration also prioritised education for the Indian community through the construction of several new Tamil schools.
"We built new Tamil schools at Ladang Saga, Ladang Linsum and Ladang Shanghai.
"I believe the best Tamil national-type school in the world is in Sendayan.
"That was my gift to the Indian community in the Rantau state constituency, to provide the best possible school for their children," he said.
He also highlighted the resolution of long-standing land issues involving residents in Gatco, which he said had remained unresolved for decades before being settled during his tenure as menteri besar.
"For 40 or 50 years, residents of Kampung Pasir did not have land titles.
"Gatco, where many Indians live, had faced land issues for 47 years. We resolved them.
"We allocated four hectares to the original settlers, two hectares to those who had purchased the land, and planned replanting with the assistance of the Rubber Industry Smallholders Development Authority," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN pledges no assessment tax hike in Negri Sembilan for 5 years
Article:
REMBAU: Barisan Nasional (BN) will not increase assessment tax in Negri Sembilan for five years if it returns to power after the state election, state BN chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
Mohamad said the state government should not rely on higher taxes to increase revenue but instead generate income through development.
"We will not increase assessment tax for the next five years.
"We want to increase the state's revenue, but not by taxing the people.
"We want to grow state revenue not by imposing higher taxes on the people, but by developing the state. Development will generate revenue, not taxing the people," he said.
Mohamad was speaking at a programme with the Indian community in Taman Intan, Rantau, last night.
The BN candidate for the Rantau state seat also said people who wanted to run small businesses should be allowed to do so, provided they complied with safety and cleanliness requirements.
"Anyone who wants to do business should be allowed to do so, as long as they observe safety and cleanliness.
"This is an era of economic challenges. If a wife is good at making nasi lemak or kuih, there is nothing wrong with her starting a small business selling them," he said.
Mohamad said the government should increase revenue through development and economic activity rather than imposing more taxes on people already burdened by the rising cost of living.
"People are already struggling with the high cost of living, yet they are expected to pay more taxes.
"We must manage the state, or the country, as a business entity. Revenue should come from business activities and development, not from taxing the people," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman loses nearly RM120,000 in non-existent investment scheme
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: A 58-year-old woman lost nearly RM120,000 after being duped by a non-existent investment scheme promising returns of RM15,000 within two hours.
District police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police received a report regarding the incident on Thursday.
He said investigations revealed that the victim was lured into the scheme after seeing an investment advertisement on Facebook on July 19.
"The syndicate's modus operandi was to offer investment packages starting from as low as RM300, promising returns of up to RM15,000 within two hours.
"The victim was asked to make several payments in stages, purportedly to release blocked investment profits," he said in a statement yesterday.
Yusof said the victim made eight money transfer transactions into eight different bank accounts, totalling RM119,599.24.
He added that the victim realised she had been cheated after failing to receive any of the promised returns despite making multiple payments.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
Yusof advised the public to remain vigilant against unauthorised or unregistered investment schemes, especially those promising lucrative returns in a short period.
"The public is also advised to follow the official social media pages of the Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) to stay informed on the latest commercial crime modus operandi.
"In addition, check bank account numbers via the Semak Mule portal before making any transactions to unknown individuals, and download the Whoscall application to reduce the risk of falling victim to scams," he said.
He also reminded scam victims to immediately contact the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 to enable prompt action to block the flow of funds into suspects' accounts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tawau floods: 335 victims still at relief centre
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A total of 335 flood victims from 96 families remain at a temporary relief centre in Tawau as of 8am today, with no casualties or untoward incidents reported so far.
The Sabah State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said all victims are still taking shelter at the Tawau Sports Complex Multipurpose Hall.
The victims are residents from Kampung Tanjung Batu Keramat, Tanjung Batu Darat, Tanjung Batu Otentik and Kampung Kinabutan Tiku Batu 6.
Continuous rain since Friday caused Tawau and surrounding areas to be affected by floods, with the disaster declared at 8.30am.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sanusi's statement reflects Pas tendency to divide people, says Fahmi
Article:
JEMPOL: Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's statement on racial issues reflects the Pas leadership's tendency to play up racial sentiments and divide society, says Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
The Pakatan Harapan communications director said such politics should not be practised, urging politicians instead to promote unity and respect the country's diversity.
"His statement reflects a widespread attitude within Pas. Previously, we saw statements on the immigrant issue from the Pas president himself.
"This is not good politics. Politics should promote unity, understand differences, and strive to unite people, not divide them," he said at a Wayang Pacak event in Taman Saujana Rompin near here last night.
Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said with National Month underway, all parties should focus on uniting the country rather than issuing statements that discriminate or divide the community.
"I hope Datuk Seri Sanusi learns a lesson and changes his attitude, though I believe that will not happen," he said.
Sanusi was previously reported as saying that Malaysia is the only
'Tanah Melayu'
for Malays, while other races have their own countries of origin, such as India and China.
The Pas central election director made the remarks during a talk in conjunction with the Negri Sembilan election on July 24.
Sanusi has since insisted that his remarks had been twisted for political gain.
He said he would take legal action, including filing lawsuits, against any individual or party that deliberately manipulated his remarks.
Fahmi also addressed a statement by Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, who claimed DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke could be a candidate for menteri besar if incumbent Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun lost in the state polls.
He noted that under the Negri Sembilan Constitution, the position of menteri besar has been reserved exclusively for Malays since its enactment, urging Asyraf Wajdi to apologise for the claim.
"I hope he apologises to the people of Negri Sembilan for the mistake he made," Fahmi said.
Meanwhile, Fahmi dismissed former Rembau member of parliament Khairy Jamaluddin's prediction that PH would only receive about 10 per cent Malay voter support in the state.
He said the political dynamics in Negri Sembilan were vastly different, expressing confidence in Aminuddin's administration, which he said had proven its ability to look after the welfare of all races.
On Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan's suggestion that the 16th General Election could be held by the end of the year, Fahmi explained that the matter had never been discussed in the Cabinet and described it as a personal opinion.
He stressed that the main focus of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the Cabinet was to stabilise the economy and navigate the effects of geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East, rather than engaging in prolonged politics or early elections.

Title: CPO futures seen lower next week on profit taking after recent rally
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Crude palm oil (CPO) futures on Bursa Malaysia Derivatives are expected to trade lower next week as profit-taking is likely to emerge after the recent rally despite crude oil prices remaining elevated.
Interband Group of Companies senior palm oil trader Jim Teh said CPO futures had climbed to about RM4,700 per tonne alongside crude oil prices, which reached about US$100 per barrel, prompting speculative buying.
However, he expects syndicate speculators to lock in gains next week, describing the market as a "yo-yo" market.
"The trading range will be between RM4,400 and RM4,500 per tonne next week," he told Bernama.
Teh said that although physical demand from key importing countries, including China, India, Pakistan, the Middle East, the European Union and the United States, would continue to support the market, ample palm oil inventories in Malaysia and Indonesia are likely to cap further gains.
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the August 2026 contract rose RM62 to RM4,591 per tonne, September 2026 added RM112 to RM4,677 per tonne, and October 2026 jumped RM125 to RM4,722 per tonne.
The November 2026 contract advanced RM123 to RM4,753 per tonne, December 2026 increased RM116 to RM4,779 per tonne, and January 2027 improved RM103 to RM4,800 per tonne.
Weekly trading volume grew to 503,068 lots from 402,028 lots in the preceding week, while open interest strengthened to 306,540 contracts on Friday from 286,716 contracts previously.
The physical CPO price for August South gained RM70 to RM4,610 per tonne.
